schemes.label: Kinds of face
schemes.note: How many classes the symmetry group divides the faces into. Falls left to right, so the table runs from the lopsided to the perfectly uniform.

columns.label: 8+ face types
columns.note: The least regular solids here, gathered so the table does not trail off into columns of one.

columns.label: 1 face type
columns.note: Every face equivalent to every other.

columns.label: Regular
columns.note: Transitive on vertices, edges and faces at once -- nothing about them can be made more uniform. The five Platonic solids and the four Kepler-Poinsot stars.

schemes.label: Kinds of vertex
schemes.note: The dual reading: how many classes of vertex. The Archimedean solids have exactly one, which is what 'vertex-transitive' means and what defines them.

columns.label: 8+ vertex types
columns.note: The least regular solids here, gathered so the table does not trail off into columns of one.

columns.label: 1 vertex type
columns.note: Every vertex equivalent to every other.

columns.label: Regular
columns.note: Transitive on vertices, edges and faces at once.

schemes.label: Symmetry group
schemes.note: The point group, from least to most symmetric. Reading across a row compares solids of similar complexity built on different symmetries.

columns.label: Cyclic
columns.note: A single rotation axis, with or without mirrors.

columns.label: Dihedral
columns.note: A principal axis with two-fold axes across it.

columns.label: Octahedral
columns.note: The symmetry of the cube and octahedron.

columns.label: Icosahedral
columns.note: The symmetry of the dodecahedron and icosahedron -- the largest a polyhedron can have.

schemes.label: Classification
schemes.note: Which closed set each solid belongs to, ordered so the regular ones come last. Compare with the other schemes: the Johnson solids spread across every face-type column, which is the table earning its keep. No column is highlighted here because regularity is split between the last two: the Platonic solids and the Kepler-Poinsot stars are equally regular, one convex and one not.

columns.label: Johnson
columns.note: The 92 convex solids with regular faces that are neither Platonic nor Archimedean.

columns.label: Catalan
columns.note: The duals of the Archimedean solids: face-transitive, but not vertex-transitive.

columns.label: Archimedean
columns.note: Vertex-transitive, with more than one kind of regular face.

schemes.label: Number of faces
schemes.note: The nearest thing here to an atomic number -- an ordering, though not an identifier: many solids share a face count, and nothing recurs at intervals of it.
